mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically for four consecutive weeks (-28.1, -19.0, -10.9, -7.1), indicating self-reinforcing momentum in foot traffic recovery driven by habituation and word-of-mouth normalization; this momentum will persist mechanically into the next four weeks absent a shock.
evidence_refs: fact:four consecutive weekly increases in RETAIL_REC
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the mean over the last 28 days, breaking the observed monotonic uptrend.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT usage has improved sharply each week (-33.7 to -8.1) as commuters resume public transport habits; once TRANSIT crosses the -10 threshold it signals near-normal commuting behavior, which mechanically increases incidental retail visits near transit hubs within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT crosses above -10 (i.e., becomes less negative than -10) on a weekly mean basis
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -33.7 to -8.1 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the subsequent two weeks after TRANSIT crosses -10, or RETAIL_REC growth is statistically indistinguishable from the prior trend.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous sustained improvement in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT reflects genuine restoration of in-person work and commuting routines, which jointly amplify retail recovery beyond what either series predicts alone, because commuters combine transit trips with shopping stops on the way to/from work.
candidate_trigger: Both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve week-on-week for at least two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -41.4 to -17.1 and TRANSIT from -33.7 to -8.1 over the snapshot window
failure_condition: The joint improvement in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT fails to produce a RETAIL_REC increase exceeding the sum of each series' independently estimated marginal effect, or RETAIL_REC declines despite both rising.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen for four consecutive weeks (-41.4 to -17.1), reflecting eased return-to-office policy settings; continued policy-driven commuting recovery mechanically raises RETAIL_REC through weekday lunch and post-work shopping trips over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved by over 24 points across four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next two weeks even though WORKPLACES continues its upward trajectory, indicating decoupling of office return from retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility is elevated and rising (56.7 to 62.4) consistent with Melbourne's spring seasonal transition, drawing discretionary outdoor leisure time away from indoor retail and recreation venues, which suppresses RETAIL_REC growth over the coming week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose to 62.4 in the most recent week, the highest in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the next week despite PARKS remaining at or above its current elevated level, indicating no substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined for four consecutive weeks (6.6 to -0.1), indicating households are spending progressively less time at home; this behavioral shift frees time and intent for out-of-home retail activity, mechanically lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 6.6 to -0.1 across four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days even as RESIDENTIAL continues to decline toward or below zero.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility turned positive and has strengthened each week (-5.6 to 13.0), signaling policy-driven normalization of essential shopping behavior; once this series remains positive for two consecutive weeks, it precedes a broader rebound into discretionary RETAIL_REC activity within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above 0 for two consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM turned positive in the last two weeks of the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks of GROCERY_PHARM sustaining positive values, indicating essential and discretionary shopping recoveries are decoupled.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES mobility rises and RESIDENTIAL mobility falls in the same week, it signals a genuine, coordinated shift away from home-based routines toward in-person work, which compounds to produce an immediate short-term boost in RETAIL_REC via combined commuting and errand trips.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES increases and RESIDENTIAL decreases within the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose and RESIDENTIAL fell concurrently in each of the last three snapshot weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows no measurable increase in the week immediately following a joint WORKPLACES rise and RESIDENTIAL fall, indicating the combined signal has no incremental effect.
